cpos.reason: Official ÜZ charging-card conditions remain publicly served: electricity customers 0.44 EUR/kWh AC and 0.48 EUR/kWh DC with 1 EUR/month; non-customers 0.49 EUR/kWh AC and 0.53 EUR/kWh DC with 6 EUR/month. Roaming 0.5995 EUR/kWh stays in the eMSP layer and is not attached to third-party physical CPOs.
Operator-wide fallback is unsafe; EVSE-level prices are now collected where verified.
EVSE-level Vaylens pricing is now collected where verified.
Verified station/EVSE snapshots are collected without operator-wide extrapolation.
Verified station/EVSE snapshots are collected without operator-wide extrapolation.

ROAD public charge flow accepts the 7-digit EVSE station identifier from BNetzA/Pluq EVSE IDs and exposes the current Pluq ad-hoc tariff without authentication. Verified German examples: DE*EFL*EV7062634 at 0.44 EUR/kWh and DE*EFL*EV0365296 at 0.51 EUR/kWh. A full collector now derives station IDs from germany-crosswalk.json and fetches exact EVSE-scoped prices; unpriced points remain visible but unranked.
Location-specific AFIR pricing is collected at exact EVSE scope.
Official Bilkraft/Eviny own-network fast-charging tariff is integrated for DC/HPC only; no AC or roaming extrapolation.
Verified station/EVSE prices are collected at exact scope.

eParkstation allows each site/owner to configure kWh, parking and blocking fees independently, so no operator-wide price is valid. Current AFIR public matching is materially incomplete. Verified exact station/point tariffs remain rankable; unknown BNetzA sites stay visible and unpriced.

OPG is a verified public CPO with its own charging card and ad-hoc QR flow. Official site-specific evidence at Klinikum Osnabrück gives 0.49 EUR/kWh with OPG E-LadeCard and 0.55 EUR/kWh ad-hoc. Do not extrapolate those values across all OPG AC/DC sites until a current universal tariff table or exact station feed is resolved.

A current exact public station-level direct price is verified at Areal Böhler Autowerk in Meerbusch: 0.49 EUR/kWh ad-hoc on six 22 kW AC points, updated 2026-05-15. Nearby inno2grid stations still publish the direct price as unknown, so 0.49 EUR/kWh must not be extrapolated network-wide. Continue resolving exact QR/backend prices per station/EVSE; unknown points remain visible and unranked.
Official 2026 own-network card, customer and ad-hoc tariffs plus blocking fee are integrated.

Official own-network AC tariff is integrated at 0.45 EUR/kWh. DC is deliberately deferred because SÜC publishes 0.54 EUR/kWh up to 50 kW and 0.59 EUR/kWh for faster/hyperchargers with different blocking thresholds; a single DC fallback would be unsafe.
Public direct.wirelane.com pages expose current EVSE-specific ad-hoc price and fees using the EVSE ID in a reproducible URL. Full collector added; no operator-wide fallback is inferred.
Qwello's public tariff site loads all tariffs from an unauthenticated tariff-view.json feed. Collector preserves EVSE-specific kWh, minute, day/night and grace-period components.

No safe universal CPO price is published; applicable chargepoint pricing is shown before charging in the E.ON Drive experience. Keep sites visible and unpriced until a reproducible public station feed is resolved; do not invent a fallback.

The official TEAG Mobil promotion valid 2026-07-23 through 2026-09-30 is exact for sessions started and billed in the TEAG Mobil app on TEAG chargepoints: the first 28 kWh cost 0.49 EUR/kWh and energy from the 29th kWh costs 0.29 EUR/kWh. Other payment/access methods use the tariff displayed at the station or in the billing system. Do not flatten the tiered app tariff into a universal CPO price and do not extrapolate it to QR/card sessions.

Official enercity guidance states that direct FlexLaden pricing is shown on the station display and that selected stations can use dynamic pricing. There is therefore no safe universal ad-hoc fallback. Resolve exact station/EVSE prices and scope future matches by physical operator because the DE*ENC prefix also contains a small number of non-enercity points.

GP JOULE publishes an official CC0 AFIR static dataset in Mobilithek. The 2026-08-30 BNetzA/AFIR comparison matches about 90% of GP JOULE sites at roughly 2 m mean distance, while current station-level ad-hoc prices demonstrably vary (for example 0.29, 0.39 and 0.55 EUR/kWh). The AFIR missing-price audit does not flag GP JOULE above its 10-point threshold, but the unmatched BNetzA remainder still prevents a network-wide completion claim. Collect exact AFIR price components per matched EVSE and leave unmatched points unranked.

Current public EVSE/station evidence shows location-specific direct prices rather than a safe operator-wide fallback: examples include 0.52 EUR/kWh AC in Duisburg/Bergisch Gladbach and 0.55 EUR/kWh on DE*HTL*E200528*1/*2 in Herne. Continue resolving the public QR/AFIR/backend price for every DE*HTL EVSE; do not extrapolate either observed price across the network.

BNetzA/AFIR matching is high but incomplete: the 2026-08-30 comparison finds about 89% of Servipark sites near Eco-Movement Contipark data. A current Servipark station-level result exposes 0.54 EUR/kWh direct payment, while other large Servipark/Contipark sites still show the ad-hoc price as unknown. Use exact AFIR/QR prices where published and keep the unmatched or unpriced remainder unranked; no 0.54 EUR/kWh network fallback is allowed.

TotalEnergies officially states that its German charging network has no uniform price: kWh prices vary by station and card and must be checked in Charge Europe or Find a Charger; some stations also have blocking fees. AFIR matching covers about 93% of TotalEnergies Charging Solutions Deutschland sites, but the 2026-09-01 AFIR audit still reports 307 TotalEnergies charge points without price data. Continue collecting exact station/EVSE prices and blocking components; never create a national fallback.

Official L-Strom.drive prices valid from 2026-01-01 are exact for the Leipziger Stadtwerke own network: regular 0.54 EUR/kWh AC and 0.64 EUR/kWh DC; eligible energy customers 0.45 EUR/kWh AC and 0.55 EUR/kWh DC; roaming 0.61/0.71 EUR/kWh remains an eMSP layer. Public QR/ad-hoc charging exists, but an exact current ad-hoc price was not found in the public tariff page, so no ad-hoc fallback is inferred.

ALDI SÜD officially publishes direct card-payment prices by charging-station class: normal stations up to 22 kW 0.29 EUR/kWh, fast stations up to 50 kW 0.44 EUR/kWh, and ultra-fast stations from 150 kW 0.47 EUR/kWh. The tariff is station-class based (an AC connector at an ultra-fast site is also 0.47 EUR/kWh). No official rule was found for a possible 51-149 kW station class, so those EVSEs must not inherit a fabricated tier.

Exact public station/EVSE examples show multiple components: DE*WWL*E68300*02 AC 22 kW at 0.56 EUR/kWh plus 0.02 EUR/min and DE*WWL*E68300*01 CCS 50 kW at 0.74 EUR/kWh plus 0.05 EUR/min. AFIR matching is high but the current AFIR missing-price audit still reports hundreds of Westfalen Weser points without price data, so no network fallback is safe.

Current public direct-payment examples for EnBW Ostwürttemberg DonauRies show station/connector-specific pricing, including 0.79 EUR/kWh on 200 kW CCS, while the separate ODR MobilityMe contract tariff is 0.55 EUR/kWh AC and 0.68 EUR/kWh DC plus time-based blocking fees. Contract and ad-hoc layers must not be conflated; continue resolving exact station/EVSE direct prices.

policy: Station-specific operators do not block the Germany pipeline unless no current price can be obtained at either operator or exact station/EVSE scope. Rank only verified exact scopes; keep unknown stations visible and unpriced. eMSP roaming prices never substitute for an unresolved physical-CPO direct price.
